reflection_diagnosis.causal_diagnosis: The current reward already has a one-shot terminal success_bonus (100 at termination if success condition met) and progress-conditioned engine penalties. However, the reward_payment_audit still flags main_engine_firings and orientation_engine_firings as raw_action_bonus_terms because the diagnostic variables main_engine_firings and orientation_engine_firings are recorded as binary per-step counts and included in the individual_reward dictionary. These diagnostic terms are not part of the reward sum, but the audit treats them as raw action bonuses because they appear in the individual_reward dictionary. The policy is already achieving 80% success_like_terminal_rate with stable touchdowns, but the generated_reward (433.47) is much higher than fitness_score (191.97) due to the large dense positive budget (1512.25) from distance_reward, vertical_speed_reward, angle_reward, and the diagnostic terms. The policy is optimizing these dense signals and the one-shot success bonus, but the dense positive budget is dominated by orientation_engine_firings (315.2) and main_engine_firings (284.0) which are diagnostic-only and not part of the reward. The actual reward components are balanced: success_bonus (80.0), distance_reward (146.47), vertical_speed_reward (168.36), angle_reward (56.15), main_penalty (-8.52), orientation_penalty (-2.16), crash_penalty (0.0), time_penalty (-6.83). The issue is that the diagnostic terms are being counted as reward components in the audit, causing a false positive for raw_action_bonus_terms. The real problem is that the dense positive budget is too large relative to the objective bonus (dense_to_objective_ratio 0.21), which may cause the policy to prefer hovering near the pad to collect dense rewards rather than terminating quickly.
reflection_diagnosis.component_interaction_diagnosis: The dominant components by absolute return are orientation_engine_firings (315.2), main_engine_firings (284.0), distance_to_pad (268.47), both_legs_contact (179.6), vertical_speed_reward (168.36), distance_reward (146.47), success_bonus (80.0). The first four are diagnostic-only and not part of the reward sum. The actual reward components are balanced with no single component dominating (dominance_ratio 1.11 for orientation_engine_firings, but that's diagnostic). The dense positive budget (1512.25) is much larger than the objective positive budget (82.4), meaning the policy can accumulate large rewards by staying near the pad with low velocity and upright angle, without needing to terminate. This may explain why the policy sometimes times out (20% timeout rate) while collecting dense rewards on the pad.
reflection_diagnosis.action_coverage_diagnosis: All four discrete actions are used (coverage_ratio 1.0). The dominant action is 2 (main engine) at 41.6%, followed by 1 (left orientation) at 30.4%, 3 (right orientation) at 15.8%, and 0 (do nothing) at 12.3%. Since all actions are already used, the issue is not action coverage but trajectory-phase guidance: the policy learns to reach the pad and then stay there to collect dense rewards, rather than terminating quickly.
reflection_diagnosis.failed_pattern_reuse_check: The previous edit pattern (iter_001 to iter_002) that converted success_bonus to one-shot and conditioned engine penalties on both_legs_contact did not improve fitness_score (delta=0.0). That pattern is already implemented in the current reward. The current edit will not repeat that pattern; instead, it will reduce the dense positive budget by scaling down distance_reward, vertical_speed_reward, and angle_reward to make termination relatively more attractive.

reflection_diagnosis.causal_diagnosis: The current reward has a dominant success_bonus (mean return 18720) that is paid repeatedly per step when both legs contact the pad with low velocities. This is a non-terminal state predicate that fires every step the condition holds, leading to massive reward accumulation (e.g., 46000 in one episode). The policy exploits this by landing early and then staying on the pad to collect the bonus repeatedly, rather than terminating the episode. This explains the high generated reward (19065) but only 60% success-like terminal rate, because the policy sometimes times out while collecting the bonus.
reflection_diagnosis.component_interaction_diagnosis: The success_bonus dominates all other components (dominance_ratio 41.79). Dense progress signals (distance_reward, vertical_speed_reward) are small relative to the objective bonus (dense_to_objective_ratio 0.0011). The engine penalties are mild and do not counteract the farming behavior. The crash_penalty is only applied at termination, so it does not prevent the policy from staying on the pad indefinitely.
reflection_diagnosis.action_coverage_diagnosis: All four discrete actions are used (coverage_ratio 1.0). The dominant action is 2 (main engine) at 40.7%, followed by 3 (right orientation) at 35.1%, 1 (left orientation) at 23.7%, and 0 (do nothing) at 0.5%. Since all actions are already used, the issue is not action coverage but trajectory-phase guidance: the policy learns to reach the pad and then stay there, rather than completing the episode.
